Model-based bioequivalence · simulation-only

Do two modelling methodologies reach the same bioequivalence decision?

A PBPK vs PopPK decision-equivalence study for metformin extended-release, sweeping the tablet's Weibull release time (T50) and asking whether a physiology-based model and a fitted population-PK model draw the same bioequivalence "safe space."

PBPK · PK-Sim PopPK · Pumas Nikita Ramwani · 2026
01

Why this matters

The formulation knob, and the decision it drives

A modified-release tablet is defined by how fast it releases drug. We turn one knob — T50, the Weibull release time — and ask how far it can drift before the product would fail a bioequivalence (BE) study.

Bioequivalence

0.80–1.25

The 90% CI of the test/reference exposure ratio (Cmax, AUC) must sit entirely inside these limits — the two one-sided tests (TOST).

Safe space

power ≥ 80%

The T50 range where a realistic study not only passes BE but has ≥ 80% power to do so. Narrower than the raw BE range.

Decision equivalence

same answer?

Do PBPK and PopPK place the safe-space boundaries in the same place and reach the same BE conclusion? That is the deliverable.

02

One study design, two methodologies

Everything is held fixed except release rate

  • 8 formulations — T50 = 1, 2, 3, 3.5, 4, 5, 6, 7 h. Reference = 3 h.
  • 24 virtual subjects, and the same 24 physiologies under every tablet → a fully paired crossover (no between-arm noise).
  • Shape held fixed (Weibull β = 1) and dose held fixed (390 mg free base) across all tablets, so any change in the profile is release-rate alone.
  • Both methodologies run on this identical design and share the same BE / VBE / safe-space statistics — so the comparison is truly apples-to-apples.

PBPK — PK-Sim

Mechanistic physiology; the tablet dissolves and the body turns it into plasma curves. The "truth."

PopPK — Pumas

Pretend you only have a sparse, noisy clinical study; fit a PK model and re-derive the same endpoints.

03

Methodology · PBPK ●

Build the physiology, dissolve the tablet

  • Start from the published, validated OSP metformin model (Hanke 2020; 39 clinical studies) — loaded and run in PK-Sim.
  • Add the extended-release tablet as a Weibull dissolution; sweep T50.
  • Simulate a 24-subject European population; export dense plasma profiles (0–24 h).
  • Per subject, take Cmax, AUC₀–t, AUC_inf by NCA — the PBPK "truth."

Weibull release

F(t) = 1 − exp( −((t − lag) / T50)β )

T50 = release time (the knob). β = shape, fixed at 1. Metformin XR is release-rate-limited, so this dissolution curve sets the whole profile.

scope Absolute exposure runs ~3–4× high vs clinic — a methodology platform, not an accuracy exercise. Being a shared offset, it cancels exactly in the test/reference ratio.

04

Methodology · PopPK ●

Pretend you only had a clinical study

  • Sparse-sample each PBPK profile at 13 realistic BE time-points and add 15% proportional assay noise.
  • Fit a Weibull-release 1-compartment model in Pumas — the depot empties by the same Weibull law the PBPK tablet uses, so the two methodologies speak the same mechanistic language.
  • Re-simulate dense profiles from the fit; re-derive the same Cmax / AUC endpoints by NCA.
  • No PBPK parameter is reused — the model is learned from the sparse noisy data alone.

Release-as-absorption

Depot(t) = Dose · exp( −((t − lag) / α)γ )

α = in-vivo release scale (the analog of T50), γ = in-vivo input shape. Clearance and volume are the drug's, not the tablet's.

Result 1 · the profiles

The fitted profiles land on the truth

06

Result 2 · the deliverable

Decision equivalence holds confirmed twice

Safe-space boundaries (power ≥ 80%, T50 in hours) from the licensed Pumas run — the two methodologies place them within ~0.05–0.15 h of each other. Confirmed by an independent joint fit.

Endpoint (n=48)PBPKPopPK
Cmax2.00–4.151.95–4.05
AUC₀–t1.00–4.601.00–4.55
Joint (Cmax & AUC₀–t)1.95–4.101.90–4.05

Cmax is the binding endpoint; the joint safe space is T50 ≈ 1.9–4.1 h by both methodologies.

07

Result 3 · the honest finding

PopPK reproduces the decision — not the mechanism

We hoped the fitted release scale α would track T50 (an in-silico IVIVC). It does not — across two licensed fits α stays flat.

PBPK T501357
α, per-arm fit1.421.691.651.71
α, joint fit1.431.681.711.76

One-compartment flip-flop non-identifiability: from a sparse read-out the model can't separate release from elimination, so the formulation effect is absorbed into apparent disposition (fitted CL 10.6→14.7, Vc 86→190 across T50) instead of α.

What it means

The BE decision transfers from mechanism to sparse data — but the in-vitro→in-vivo release mapping does not.

Recovering the release mechanism needs a mechanistic model — which is exactly where PBPK earns its keep over PopPK. A cleaner, more useful result than a forced IVIVC.

08

Under the hood

The ratio that drives it all

09

What we learned

Takeaways

1 · Decision equivalence

A sparse-data PopPK analysis reaches the same BE safe space as the mechanistic PBPK model (T50 ≈ 1.9–4.1 h), robust across fitting strategies.

2 · Mechanism ≠ decision

PopPK does not recover the release mapping from sparse data (flip-flop). The formulation effect hides in apparent disposition.

3 · Where PBPK wins

Mechanistic questions (release, IVIVC, extrapolation) need the physiology-based model — PopPK can't back them out of a clinical-style study.

4 · Same-language matters

Using the identical Weibull release on both sides made the comparison clean and let the PopPK profiles reproduce the PBPK ones to ~3%.

10

Scope, limitations & what's next

Honest edges

  • Methodology platform. Absolute exposure ~3–4× high; valid because BE is relative and the offset cancels. Not for absolute-exposure claims.
  • One compartment. Most published metformin PopPK models are two-compartment; 1-cmt is a transparent choice here and the natural sensitivity to extend.
  • AUC_inf is unstable for the slow, flip-flop tablets — AUC₀–t is the primary AUC endpoint.
  • Next: 2-compartment sensitivity; type-I-error at the boundaries; a real dissolution-anchored T50.

Reproducibility

Two self-contained Julia/Pumas pipelines (per-arm baseline + joint IVIVC variant), run on licensed Pumas; open-package steps and a license-free cross-check included.

Refs: Hanke 2020 (metformin PBPK) · Morris 2026 (safe space + type-I error) · FDA NDA 212595 (within-subject CV) · Bois & Brochot 2024.
